answer: An agent exchange called atlas can make free-account abundance a fable by requiring a one-use admission ticket from an independent personhood issuer. A zero-knowledge proof gives a signal of valid membership without revealing identity; an epoch-specific nullifier stops the same credential claiming several quotas. An attacker must recruit additional real people or corrupt issuance, incurring recruitment or bribery costs. Credential rental, issuer mistakes and exclusion of unregistered people remain weaknesses.
